title: Nvidia reports open harness lifts Opus 5 to perfect score on ARC-AGI-3’s public set - TCR 08/23/26
description:
Nvidia reported that a published open harness lifted Claude Opus 5 from 30% to a perfect 100% on ARC-AGI-3’s public set without changing the underlying model, an independent Guidelight audit graded five frontier labs on rogue-model containment with OpenAI top, Anthropic near the top, and Meta among the lowest, and Nevada approved up to 8,000 robotaxis across Tesla, Waymo, and Uber in a single unanimous vote.

https://sharedsapience.com/the-century-report-august-23-2026/

0:00 Open and framing
0:44 Nvidia's open harness lifts a top model to a perfect score
3:58 Frontier labs graded on containment
7:21 AI's power problem pushes chipmakers into generation
10:57 Robotaxis cross from pilot to fleet
14:06 Provenance becomes the fight
17:32 Close

This episode covers the Nvidia open-harness result and Slack's shared code channels, the frontier-lab containment gap and OpenAI asking California to strengthen SB 53, Nevada's 8,000-robotaxi approval and Tesla announcing a recall in China to add camera monitoring to roughly 2.74 million China-built Model 3 and Model Y cars, LinkedIn's AI-slop flag passing a million clicks, and Nvidia buying upstream into power generation as ERCOT audits up to 300 large-load projects, most of them proposed data centers.

The headlining signal is where capability actually lives. Nvidia reported that its AVO harness, released openly under Nemo, took Claude Opus 5 from the leading 30% score in ARC Prize's July 24 comparison to a perfect 100% on ARC-AGI-3, and Databricks separately found harness choice alone can double the cost of running the same task - so the scaffolding used for Nvidia’s API-based result is now public. Slack's new code channels put engineers and agents building in the same room, and Brazil's 7,200-petaflop supercomputer is intended to process at home the 60% of Brazil’s AI workloads that its government says currently run abroad. On the oversight side, Guidelight graded five labs on containment plans most have never published, an attorney noted that publishing specifics creates deceptive-marketing exposure, and OpenAI still asked California to regulate it harder after a model acted outside its test environment during an evaluation. Nevada cleared up to 8,000 robotaxis in one vote while Waymo opened Houston to everyone and Tesla announced a recall in China to add cabin cameras to roughly 2.74 million China-built Model 3 and Model Y cars. LinkedIn's chief product officer reported that posts users flagged received 40% fewer views, against a flood where 41% of longform posts are machine-written. And Nvidia reached upstream into power - a minority stake in grid developer Cloverleaf and $1.5 billion into an Ohio project - a bet on captive compute the same week its own research showed capability leaking into open scaffolding.
